note: How FIELD OBSERVATIONS (counts, % damage) are read: economic threshold levels (ETL) transcribed from the national IPM Package for Rice (NCIPM / DPPQ&S, 2014, Table 3.1.2, p. 9). Transcribed by the integration lead on 2026-10-08 and NOT yet verified by Member A, so every rule stays PLACEHOLDER. These are not weather rules (those are pest_rules.json, Member A) and not observations (those come from an observation source). An ETL is the level at which management action is advised; it is not a probability of outbreak. Multi-part ETLs that need two measurements together (brown spot, sheath blight, sheath rot, tungro) are left out rather than simplified.

severity_from_etl.note: Engineering mapping, not an agronomic finding: a value below the ETL's low end counts as low severity, inside the ETL range as moderate, at or above its high end as high. Only used when a record gives a measured value but no severity of its own.
